metadata.source: CDS SIMBAD Astronomical Database (Strasbourg astronomical Data Center)
metadata.description: Verified astrometric, photometric, and spectroscopic parameters for benchmark stellar targets.

records.name: Sirius A
records.description: The brightest star in Earth's night sky, orbited by a faint white dwarf companion (Sirius B).

records.name: Betelgeuse
records.description: A massive red supergiant nearing the end of its nuclear life cycle, destined to explode as a core-collapse supernova.

records.name: Vega
records.description: The historical baseline standard for the zero-point of the astronomical magnitude system, surrounded by a circumstellar dust disk.

records.name: Rigel
records.description: An intensely luminous blue supergiant shining with over 100,000 times the radiant power of the Sun.

records.name: Proxima Centauri
records.description: The closest known star to our Solar System, hosting at least two confirmed exoplanets (Proxima b and Proxima d).

records.name: Polaris
records.description: Earth's northern celestial pole star, a multiple star system anchored by a Classical Cepheid variable pulsating every 3.97 days.
